body:
Handoff and continuity rules for TermAl (Termal::Fable2, 2026-11-13 at about 03:40Z). They answer Greg (Asistant 588693a8 #1497/#1498/#1500): „reguly przekazywania dalej sesji musza byc precyzyjne”, after every TermAl session sat idle with a large Greg-reported backlog.
CAUSE: (a) The coordinator (Fable2) left free Sol/Opus coders without assignments. (b) The integration owner (Opus2) was the only path to placements and was quiet after a landing, so authors waited. (c) Sending mail by a listed display name routes to a domain mailbox and does not wake the recipient (w-ee0454f76b19).
RULES, with no new gates:
1. WHO hands to WHOM. Coordinator → coder: assignment. Coder → Opus2: READY or a placement request. Opus2 → coder: GO, or a result. Coder → coordinator: a done or blocked state. Coordinator → Greg: only through Asistant.
2. TRIGGER. Every message ends with NEXT: <owner> <action>. Whoever finishes a step starts or requests the next one in the same turn. A coder that finishes an item tells the coordinator, who assigns the next ready item in that turn.
3. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. The recipient replies on its next turn: either "taken" plus an ETA, or why not. A send receipt is not delivery. durableButNotWoken means NOT woken: resend natively at once. Always address by native id (session-N, or host:UUID::session-N).
4. NO REACTION. After 20 min, the sender pings once natively. After 40 min, it escalates to the coordinator, who reassigns or takes over and records why.
5. PARALLELISM. A running FULL never blocks reviews, author focused runs on other runners, or new code writing. Opus2 places them alongside each other, within the Central budget.
6. WATCHDOG. Fable2 has a 30-min cron, at :13 and :43, that checks every coder has work or a named next owner, and assigns from the ready Greg-reported backlog.
